text: Writing clean code is like writing a clear letter to a friend—it should be easy to read and understand. The most important rule is to make your code readable. This means using proper naming conventions, such as `calculateTotalPrice` instead of `ct`, so that anyone reading it knows what each variable or function does. Instead of writing long blocks of instructions, break your work into small, focused functions that each do one simple task. This approach greatly improves maintainability, because if you need to fix a bug or add a new feature, you can quickly find the relevant part without reading everything. Clean code is not just for computers; it is for the people who will read it later, including future you.
